newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on soybean gains, Witter outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on soybean gains, Witter outlook.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a late rally in soybean futures triggered in part by a bullish soybean stocks forecast by Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel, traders said.
"Witter cut the carryout and I think that might have produced a little support also," a trader said.
Gidel pegged 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks at 125 million bushels, below USDA's current outlook for 155 million. USDA Wednesday will release its February Supply/Demand Report.
A slowdown in soybean/corn spreading also was cited as a mild supportive influence for corn futures.

"We have seen a lot of people buying beans and selling corn and that's losing its luster," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "There's pretty good (domestic and export) usage at $2.70."
There was no fresh news overnight to drive the market one way or another, traders said.
Corn closed one to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 2-1/4 at $2.71. May was up 1-3/4 cents at $2.69-3/4.

"The weather is good in South America and here and we were a little lower (on the open) on follow through," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. Corn sagged quietly on the open but there were no signs of aggressive selling interest and the market gently eased above the $2.70 mark and broke through minor selling resistance at that level in late dealings.
Technicians cited first support in March corn at $2.67-1/4 and second support at $2.63. The session low for March was $2.68-1/4.
First resistance was at $2.71-1/2 and second was at $2.75-3/4. The session high was $2.72-1/4.
Early Friday the four- and 20-day moving averages continued to give off bearish signals for the March through July contracts, chartists reported.
Dean Witter bought three million bushels of March and SAK Futures bought two million March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, below the 49,834 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Continental Grain bought 2,000 December $2.80 calls, sold 2,000 December $3.30 calls and sold 2,000 September $2.40 puts, traders said.
LFG Futures sold 1,000 December $2.80 calls, bought 1,000 December $3.30 calls and bought 1,000 September $2.40 puts at three cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 16,200 traded Thursday.
